glosses: To follow something in sequence or time.

examples.text: Autumn succeeds summer.

glosses: To replace or supplant someone in order vis-à-vis an office, position, or title.

examples.text: The king's eldest son succeeds his father on the throne.

glosses: To come after or follow; to be subsequent or consequent; (often with to).

examples.text: Her arms were like legs of mutton, her breasts like giant cabbages; her face, broad and fleshy, gave you an impression of almost indecent nakedness, and vast chin succeeded to vast chin.

glosses: To come in the place of another person, thing, or event; to come next in the usual, natural, or prescribed course of things; to follow; hence, to come next in the possession of anything; (often with to).

examples.text: Following the death of his mother, he succeeded to the throne.
So, if the issue of the elder son succeed before the younger, the crown (or: property) falls to me.

examples.text: The persecution of any righteous practice has never succeeded in the face of history; in fact, it can expedite the collapse of the persecutory regime.
